confirmed.claim: Aiuvarin's printed elf-feat access is not implemented. The heritage record carries no `extraAncestryFeatTraits`, and that field is the ONLY route the ancestry-slot gate has for opening another ancestry's list, so all 52 elf-trait ancestry feats (22 of them level <= 3) are unselectable in Bellphor's ancestry feat slot. The aiuvarin half works (7 feats, matched by `her.traits`); the elf half reaches nobody.

The ancestry-feat MENU that Ancestral Paragon opens — the route by which Bellphor actually owns Intuitive Cooperation — is narrower than the app's own feat-slot gate: it filters strictly on `build.ancestryId`, so it offers halfling feats only. refuted.claim: Domain Initiate's domain picker does not enforce "a different domain each time", so Bellphor's level-2 class feat could be answered Family — the same domain his doctrine's Domain Initiate already took. The picker offers Family again with no reason shown, accepts it, and the engine then silently merges the two takings, spending a class feat for nothing.
refuted.why: The observed symptom is real but the claim MIS-READS THE ENGINE, and the proposal as written is INERT — no player-visible change. buildChoiceOptions RETURNS BEFORE the greying code the claim cites. Verbatim, src/rules/build.ts:1728-1739: `export function buildChoiceOptions(recordId, def, build, content, character, slotKey?): NarrowedOption[] {` then `  if (def.kind === 'domains') {` / `    const featId = slotKey ? build.featPicks?.[slotKey] : undefined;` / `    return domainPoolForChoice(build, content, featId, def.domainPool).map((d) => ({ value: d, label: cap(d) }));` / `  }`. The `const claimed = def.distinctAcrossTakes ? answersInOtherTakes(...)` line is 1774 and markClaimed 1775-1782 — 35 lines AFTER the domains branch has already returned. core.json feats['domain-initiate'].choice.kind is 'domains', so neither `claimed` nor `markClaimed` is ever reached for this record. MEASURED, not inferred: with build.featPicks {'2:class:0':'domain-initiate','4:class:0':'domain-initiate'} and featChoices['2:class:0']='sun', I called buildChoiceOptions('domain-initiate', def, …, '4:class:0') twice — with the record's real choice def and with {...def, distinctAcrossTakes:true}, i.e. exactly the value the proposal's effect-backfill row would install. BOTH returned the identical unmarked list [{family,Family},{might,Might},{nature,Nature},{sun,Sun}] — no `disabled` key on any option, flag or no flag, and this is the slot-vs-slot case the CURRENT answersInOtherTakes already covers, so the proposal's engine patch is not what is missing either. Control in the same run: blessing-of-the-sun-gods (kind 'array', flag already set) returned {"value":"sun","label":"Sun — Dazzling Flash","disabled":"Already chosen by another Blessing of the Sun Gods — each time, choose a different one."} — proving the machinery works only on the paths that reach line 1774. I also enumerated every reader of the flag (`grep -rn distinctAcrossTakes src/`): build.ts:1774 is the ONLY one (plus Builder.tsx:2259 for the unrelated spellFilter.distinctAcrossTakes), so no second surface rescues the row. Separately, the granted taking's picker never consults it at all: Builder.tsx:644 calls `domainPoolForChoice(build, content, grantedId, def.domainPool)` directly, bypassing buildChoiceOptions entirely. What IS confirmed, and should be re-filed with a correct fix: print (public/core-descriptions.json feats/domain-initiate) says "**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, selecting a different domain each time and gaining its domain spell"; the record carries no distinctAcrossTakes while 37 others do, including blessing-of-the-sun-gods and greater-sun-blessing which print the same sentence; and answering both takings 'family' MEASURES as one feat row (domain-initiate@2, choice family), focus {"current":1,"max":1}, repertoire {"1":["soothing-words"]}. A working fix must ALSO route the kind:'domains' branch through markClaimed (move the branch below line 1782, or apply markClaimed inside it) and give the granted picker at Builder.tsx:644 the same treatment — neither of which the proposal does. Note this finding is largely subsumed by doctrine-domain-initiate-swallowed-by-own-pick: fix that one and the duplicate answer stops silently costing a class feat.
